sentences.text:
Applicant :- Om Prakash
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Civil Secrt. Lko.

And Another
Counsel for Applicant :- O.P. Tiwari,Om Shankar Tiwari
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Subhash Vidyarthi,J.
1.
Heard Sri O.P. Tiwari, the learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Rishikesh Verma, the learned AGA for the State and perused the records.

2. By means of the instant application filed under Section 482 Cr.P.C., the applicant has sought quashing of the judgment and order dated 08.08.2023 passed by the Session Judge, Unnao in Criminal Revision No. 8 of 2023, Manoj Kumari v. State of U.P., filed by the opposite party no. 2,
whereby the Revisional Court has set aside the order dated 14.11.2022 passed by the Judicial Magistrate, Safipur, Unnao accepting the final report dated 01.04.2019 submitted by the Investigating Officer in relation of Case Crime No. 271 of 2018, under Sections 376, 504, 506 IPC,
Police Station Safipur, District Unnao.
3.

entities.text: Manoj Kumari v. State of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The submission of the learned counsel for the applicant is that even earlier also, a final report was submitted on 22.10.2018.

The opposite party no. 2 had filed a protest, which was accepted by means Om Prakash vs State Of U.P Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Civil ... on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38675579/
1 of an order dated 20.12.2018 and the matter was sent to the Investigating Officer for conducting further investigation.

entities.text: Om Prakash vs State Of U.P Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Civil
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Investigating Officer again submitted a final report on 01.04.2019.

The opposite party no. 2 had put in appearance before the trial court on 26.04.2019 but thereafter numerous dates were fixed but the opposite party no. 2 did not file any protest petition and for this reason, the final report was accepted.

4. The revisional court has recorded in the impugned order that the matter was transferred to the court of Judicial Magistrate, Safipur and no notice of transfer of the case was given to the informant and, therefore, the opposite party no. 2 could not appear and file a protest petition in the trial court.

5. The learned Session Judge has allowed the revision and set aside the order dated 14.11.2022 passed by the trial court accepting the final report in absence of the informant-opposite party no. 2 and has directed the trial court to give an opportunity to the opposite party no. 2 to submit a protest application and thereafter dispose of the same after giving an opportunity of hearing to the parties.

6. As the revisional court has allowed the revision on the ground that the order dated 14.11.2022 had been passed by the trial court in absence of the opposite party no. 2, which was for the reason that the opposite party no. 2 could not get any intimation of the transfer of the case to the court of Judicial Magistrate, Safipur, and the revisional court has directed the trial court to pass order afresh after giving opportunity of hearing to the parties, I am of the view that there is no illegality in the order dated 08.08.2020 warranting interference of this Court in exercise of inherent power under Section 482 Cr.P.C..
7.
The applicant lacks merit and the same is accordingly rejected.
